requirements.text: ESAs which are intentional RF transmitters and which have not received type approval in conjunction with a vehicle manufacturer shall be supplied with suitable installation guidelines.

The electrical/electronic sub-assembly (ESA) conforming to a type approved under this Regulation shall have an approval mark described in paragraph 5.3. affixed to it, except that no marking is required for electrical/electronic systems built into vehicles which are approved as units.

The vehicle and its electrical/electronic system(s) or ESA(s) shall be designed, constructed and fitted in such a way as to enable the vehicle, in normal conditions of use, to comply with the requirements of this Regulation.
The ESA(s) shall be tested for radiated and conducted emissions, for immunity to radiated and conducted disturbances.

When measurements are made using the method described in Annex 7, the limits shall be 62 to 52 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band, this limit decreasing logarithmically with frequencies above 30 MHz, and 52 to 63 dB microvolts/m in the 75 to 400 MHz band, this limit increasing logarithmically with frequencies above 75 MHz as shown in Appendix 6 to this Regulation.
When measurements are made using the method described in Annex 7, in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band the limit shall remain constant at 63 dB microvolts/m.
The ESA representative of its type shall have measured values, expressed in dB microvolts/m, below the type approval limits.

When measurements are made using the method described in Annex 8, the limits shall be 52 to 42 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band, this limit decreasing logarithmically with frequencies above 30 MHz, and 42 to 53 dB microvolts/m in the 75 to 400 MHz band, this limit increasing logarithmically with frequencies above 75 MHz as shown in Appendix 7.
When measurements are made using the method described in Annex 8, the limit in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band shall remain constant at 53 dB microvolts/m.
The ESA representative of its type shall have a measured value, expressed in dB microvolts/m, below the type approval limits.
The emission of ESA representative of its type shall be tested by the method(s) according to ISO 7637-2 as described in Annex 10 for the levels given in Table 1.
The ESA representative of its type shall be tested for immunity to electromagnetic radiation by the method(s) as described in Annex 9.
The ESA representative of its type shall be tested for immunity to electromagnetic radiation such that test severity in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band are given in Table 2a.

The ESA representative of its type shall be tested for immunity to electromagnetic radiation such that test severity for the minimum test Level over the whole 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band is as given in Table 2b.

While tests are performed in accordance with Annex 9, the ESA representative of its type shall be considered as complying with immunity requirements if there is no degradation of performance of "immunity related functions".

The immunity of ESA representative of this type shall be tested by the method(s) according to ISO 16750-2 for starting profile and ISO 7637-2 for pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b, as described in Annex 10, with the test levels given in Tables 3a and 3b.
The starting profile shall be tested according to the functional status classification as defined in ISO 16750-1.
The Functional Performance Status Classification (FPSC) as in ISO 7637-1 shall be applied for pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b.

For the 12 V system starting profile (ISO 16750-2, test level II, 10 pulses), an ESA that shall be operational during engine start phases shall reach functional status class B if it performs immunity-related functions and class D if it does not, and any other ESA shall reach class C, as given in Table 3a; the starting profile applies only to ESAs that may be installed in vehicles with an internal combustion engine started by a 12 V / 24 V starter motor.

For the 24 V system starting profile (ISO 16750-2, test level II, 10 pulses), an ESA that shall be operational during engine start phases shall reach functional status class B if it performs immunity-related functions and class D if it does not, and any other ESA shall reach class C, as given in Table 3a; the starting profile applies only to ESAs that may be installed in vehicles with an internal combustion engine started by a 12 V / 24 V starter motor.

For pulse 1, the ESA shall meet immunity test level -75 V (12V system) or -450 V (24V system) for 500 pulses with FPSC III for functions related to immunity and FPSC III for functions not related to immunity as specified in Table 3b.

For pulse 2a, the ESA shall meet immunity test level +37 V (12V system) or +37 V (24V system) for 500 pulses with FPSC I for functions related to immunity and FPSC III for functions not related to immunity as specified in Table 3b.

For pulse 2b, the ESA shall meet immunity test level +10 V (12V system) or +20 V (24V system) for 10 pulses with FPSC II for functions related to immunity and FPSC III for functions not related to immunity as specified in Table 3b.

For pulse 3a, the ESA shall meet immunity test level -112 V (12V system) or -150 V (24V system) for 1 h with FPSC I for functions related to immunity and FPSC III for functions not related to immunity as specified in Table 3b.

For pulse 3b, the ESA shall meet immunity test level +75 V (12V system) or +150 V (24V system) for 1 h with FPSC I for functions related to immunity and FPSC III for functions not related to immunity as specified in Table 3b.
RF transmitters shall be tested in the transmit mode.
Spurious emissions of RF transmitters shall be subject to this Regulation.
The ESA shall meet its immunity requirements under the test conditions according to ISO 11452-1.
The ESA under test shall be switched on and shall be stimulated to be in normal operation condition during the immunity test.
The ESA under test shall be arranged as defined in Annex 9 unless individual test methods dictate otherwise.
The measurements shall be made in the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency range with frequency steps according to ISO 11452-1.

The test signal modulation shall be AM (amplitude modulation), with 1 kHz modulation and 80 per cent modulation depth in the 20 to 400 MHz frequency range, if not otherwise agreed between Technical Service and ESA manufacturer.

The test signal modulation shall be PM2 (pulse modulation type 2), Ton 3 µs, period 3,333 µs in the 2,700 to 3,100 MHz frequency range, if not otherwise agreed between Technical Service and ESA manufacturer.

The test signal modulation shall be PM3 (pulse modulation type 3), Ton 500 µs, period 1,000 µs in the 380 to 2,700 MHz and the 3,100 to 6,000 MHz frequency ranges, if not otherwise agreed between Technical Service and ESA manufacturer.

For immunity against transient disturbances conducted along 12/24 V supply lines, the test pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b according to ISO 7637-2 shall be applied to the supply lines as well as to other connections of the ESA which may be operationally connected to supply lines.

For immunity against transient disturbances conducted along 12/24 V supply lines, the starting profile according to ISO 16750-2 shall be applied to the supply lines as well as to other connections of the ESA which may be operationally connected to supply lines; ESAs exclusively reserved for mounting on electric vehicles (vehicles without a 12 V / 24 V starter motor) are not subject to the starting profile.

The ESA shall limit emission of transient conducted disturbances on 12/24 V supply lines, measured according to ISO 7637-2 on the supply lines as well as on other connections of the ESA which may be operationally connected to supply lines.

The external surface of vehicles shall not exhibit, directed outwards, any pointed or sharp parts or any projections of such shape, dimensions, direction or hardness as to be likely to increase the risk or seriousness of bodily injury to a person hit by the external surface or brushing against it in the event of a collision.
The external surface of vehicles shall not exhibit, directed outwards, any part likely to catch on pedestrians, cyclists or motor cyclists.

No protruding part of the external surface shall have a radius of curvature less than 2.5 mm, except that this requirement shall not apply to parts of the external surface which protrude less than 5 mm.
The outward facing angles of parts of the external surface which protrude less than 5 mm shall be blunted, save where such parts protrude less than 1.5 mm.
Protruding parts of the external surface, made of a material of hardness not exceeding 60 shore A, may have a radius of curvature less than 2.5 mm.

The hardness of protruding parts of the external surface made of a material of hardness not exceeding 60 shore A shall be measured with the component as installed on the vehicle, and where it is impossible to carry out a hardness measurement by the Shore A procedure, comparable measurements shall be used for evaluation.

Added ornaments which project more than 10 mm from their support shall retract, become detached or bend over under a force of 10 daN exerted at their most salient point in any direction in a plane approximately parallel to the surface on which they are mounted.
The provisions of paragraph 6.1.1 shall not apply to ornaments on radiator grilles, to which only the general requirements of paragraph 5. shall apply.
After the ornaments are retracted, detached or bent over, the remaining projections shall not project more than 10 mm.
After the ornaments are retracted, detached or bent over, the remaining projections shall in any case satisfy the provisions of paragraph 5.2.

When the 10 daN force is applied to added ornaments which project more than 10 mm from their support, a flat-ended ram of not more than 50 mm diameter shall be used, or where this is not possible, an equivalent method shall be used.
If an added ornament is mounted on a base, the base shall be regarded as belonging to the ornament and not to the supporting surface.
Protective strips or shielding on the external surface shall not be subject to the requirements of paragraph 6.1.1.; however, they shall be firmly secured to the vehicle.

Gaps between fixed or movable elements, including those forming part of air intake or outlet grilles and radiator grilles, shall not be subject to the requirements of paragraph 5.4., provided that the distance between consecutive elements does not exceed 40 mm and provided that the grilles and gaps have a functional purpose.
For gaps of between 40 mm and 25 mm the radii of curvature of the elements shall be 1 mm or more.
If the distance between two consecutive elements is equal to or less than 25 mm, the radii of curvature of external faces of the elements shall not be less than 0.5 mm.
The distance between two consecutive elements of grilles and gaps shall be determined according to the method described in paragraph 4. of Annex 3 to this Regulation.
The junction of the front with the side faces of each element forming a grille or gap shall be blunted.
The ends of the bumpers shall be turned in towards the external surface in order to minimize the risk of fouling.

The requirement for the ends of the bumpers to be turned in towards the external surface shall be considered satisfied if either the bumper is recessed or integrated within the bodywork, or the end of the bumper is turned in so that it is not contactable by a 100 mm sphere and the gap between the bumper end and the surrounding bodywork does not exceed 20 mm.

When the line of the bumper which corresponds to the outline contour of the car vertical projection is on a rigid surface, that surface shall have a minimum radius of curvature of 5 mm at all its points lying from the contour line to 20 mm inward, within the zone lying from the contour line to 20 mm inward which is situated between and in front (or rear in case of the rear bumper) of tangential points with the contour line of two vertical planes each forming with the longitudinal plane of symmetry of the vehicle an angle of 15° (see Fig. 1).

When the line of the bumper which corresponds to the outline contour of the car vertical projection is on a rigid surface, that surface shall have a minimum radius of curvature of 2.5 mm in all other cases.

The requirement of paragraph 6.5.2. shall not apply to parts on or of the bumper or to bumper insets which have a projection of less than 5 mm, with special reference to joint covers and jets for headlamp washers.
The outward facing angles of parts on or of the bumper or of bumper insets which have a projection of less than 5 mm shall be blunted, save where such parts protrude less than 1.5 mm.
The projection shall not exceed 40 mm in the case of door or luggage compartment handles and 30 mm in all other cases.

Folds in body panels may have a radius of curvature of less than 2.5 mm only if it is not less than one-tenth of the height "H" of the projection, measured in accordance with the method described in paragraph 1. of Annex 3 to this Regulation.
Air intake and outlet flaps shall meet the requirements of paragraphs 5.2., 5.3. and 5.4. above in all positions of use.

Supporting brackets provided by the vehicle manufacturer for registration plates shall comply with the requirements of paragraph 5.4. of this Regulation if they are contactable by a 100 mm diameter sphere when a registration plate is fitted in accordance with the vehicle manufacturer's recommendation.

Radio receiving and transmitting aerials shall be fitted to the vehicle in such a way that if their unattached end is less than 2 m from the road surface in any position of use specified by the manufacturer of the aerial, the unattached end shall be inside the zone bounded by the vertical planes which are 10 cm inside the extreme outer edge of the vehicle as defined in paragraph 2.7. of this Regulation.

Aerials shall be so fitted to the vehicle, and if necessary their unattached ends so restricted, that no part of the aerials protrude beyond the extreme outer edge of the vehicle as defined in paragraph 2.7. of this Regulation.

Shafts of aerials may have radii of curvature of less than 2.5 mm; however, the unattached ends of aerials shall be fitted with fixed cappings, the radii of curvature of which are not less than 2.5 mm.
The bases of aerials shall not project more than 40 mm when determined according to the procedure of paragraph 2. of Annex 3 to this Regulation.

Paragraphs 6.17.4. and 6.17.4.1. above shall not apply to aerials located behind the vertical transversal plane passing through the "R" point of the driver, provided that the maximum projection of the aerial including its housing does not exceed 70 mm when determined according to the procedure of paragraph 2. of Annex 3 to this Regulation.

If the aerial is located behind the vertical transversal plane passing through the "R" point of the driver but projects more than 70 mm, paragraph 6.17.4.1. above shall apply using a projection limit of 70 mm instead of 40 mm.
After each impact test made in accordance with the conditions and procedure specified in annex 3 to this Regulation, the lighting and signalling devices shall continue to operate correctly.
After each impact test made in accordance with the conditions and procedure specified in annex 3 to this Regulation, the lighting and signalling devices shall remain visible.

Where the adjustment of the factory-fitted lighting devices is disturbed after each impact test made in accordance with the conditions and procedure specified in annex 3 to this Regulation, it shall be permitted to correct it to conform to the required specifications, provided this can be done by the normal means of adjustment.

After each impact test made in accordance with the conditions and procedure specified in annex 3 to this Regulation, bulbs of the lighting and signalling devices shall be permitted to be replaced in the event of filament failure.
After each impact test made in accordance with the conditions and procedure specified in annex 3 to this Regulation, the caps of the vehicle's fuel system shall be operable in the normal manner.

After each impact test made in accordance with the conditions and procedure specified in annex 3 to this Regulation, the vehicle's fuel and cooling systems shall have neither leaks nor constricted fluid passages which prevent normal functioning.

After each impact test made in accordance with the conditions and procedure specified in annex 3 to this Regulation, the sealing devices of the vehicle's fuel and cooling systems and the caps of the vehicle's cooling system shall be operable in the normal manner.
The vehicle's bonnet (hood), boot lid (trunk lid) and doors shall be operable in the normal manner after each impact test made in accordance with the conditions and procedure specified in annex 3.
The side doors of the vehicle shall not be able to open under the effect of the impact test made in accordance with the conditions and procedure specified in annex 3.

The vehicle's exhaust system shall not suffer any damage or displacement which would prevent its normal function after each impact test made in accordance with the conditions and procedure specified in annex 3.

The vehicle's propulsion, suspension (including tyres), steering and braking systems shall remain in adjustment and shall operate in a normal manner after each impact test made in accordance with the conditions and procedure specified in annex 3.
The reference height shall be 445 mm.
The longitudinal impact test shall consist of two impacts on the front surface and two impacts on the rear surface of the vehicle.
For the impacts on the front and rear surfaces, the median plane of the impactor for the second impact shall be at a distance of at least 300 mm from the first impact.
In the longitudinal impact test, the vehicle shall be impacted at a speed of 4 km/h +0.25/-0.

The corner impact test shall consist of an impact at one front corner and an impact at one rear corner of the vehicle with the vehicle at unladen weight (see paragraph 3.1.3. of the Regulation), and an impact at the other front corner and the other rear corner with the vehicle at the weight given in paragraph 3.1.4. of the Regulation.
In the corner impact test, plane A of the impactor shall make an angle of 60 ± 5º with the longitudinal median plane of the vehicle.
In the corner impact test, the vehicle shall be impacted at a speed of 2.5 km/h +0.1/-0.
If the protective devices include self-restoring materials, the permitted recovery time between tests shall be as stated by the manufacturer.

The lighting and light-signalling devices shall be so fitted that under normal conditions of use as defined in paragraphs 2.3.10., 2.3.10.1. and 2.3.10.2. and notwithstanding any vibrations to which the lighting and light-signalling devices may be subjected, the lighting and light-signalling devices retain the characteristics prescribed by this Regulation.

The lighting and light-signalling devices shall be so fitted that under normal conditions of use as defined in paragraphs 2.3.10., 2.3.10.1. and 2.3.10.2. and notwithstanding any vibrations to which the lighting and light-signalling devices may be subjected, the lighting and light-signalling devices enable the vehicle to comply with the requirements of this Regulation.

The lighting and light-signalling devices shall prevent the lamps from being inadvertently maladjusted under normal conditions of use as defined in paragraphs 2.3.10., 2.3.10.1. and 2.3.10.2. and notwithstanding any vibrations to which the lighting and light-signalling devices may be subjected.

For all light-signalling devices, including those mounted on the side panels, the reference axis of the lamp when fitted to the vehicle shall be parallel to the bearing plane of the vehicle on the road, with a tolerance of ±3° allowed in each direction.

For all light-signalling devices other than side retro-reflectors and side-marker lamps, the reference axis of the lamp when fitted to the vehicle shall be parallel to the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle, with a tolerance of ±3° allowed in each direction.
For all light-signalling devices, including those mounted on the side panels, any specific instructions as regards fitting laid down by the manufacturer shall be complied with.
The lamps shall have substantially identical photometric characteristics, except that this shall not apply to a matched pair of a function and/or an AFS.
The lamps incorporating a manufacturer logo shall have only two lateral logos (one on each side) or one central logo fitted on the rear of the vehicle.
The lamps incorporating a manufacturer logo shall not include any logos that are not vehicle manufacturer or body manufacturer logos.

While lamps are grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated with one another, the lamps shall fulfill all requirements regarding colour, position, orientation, geometric visibility, electrical connections and other requirements, if any.
While all other functions with which a lamp is grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated are switched OFF, the lamp shall fulfill the photometric and colorimetric requirements.

When a front or rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with one or more other function(s) which can be switched ON together with them, and the reciprocally incorporated function(s) and the front or rear position lamps are switched ON, the front or rear position lamp shall fulfill the requirements regarding colour of each of these other functions.
Stop lamps and direction-indicator lamps shall not be reciprocally incorporated.

The single lamps as defined in paragraph 2.14.11.1., subparagraph (a), the apparent surface of which is composed of two or more distinct parts, shall be installed in such a way that either the total area of the projection of the distinct parts of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis on a plane tangent to the exterior surface of the outer lens and perpendicular to the reference axis shall occupy not less than 60 per cent of the smallest quadrilateral circumscribing the projection of the said apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis; or the minimum distance between the facing edges of two adjacent/tangential distinct parts of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis shall not exceed 75 mm when measured perpendicularly to the reference axis, except that these requirements shall not apply to a single retro-reflector.
Single lamps as defined in paragraph 2.4.11.1., subparagraph (d) shall fulfil the requirements of paragraph 5.7.2.1.

Where two or more lamps and/or two or more separate apparent surfaces are included into the same lamp body and/or have a common outer lens, they shall not be considered as an interdependent lamp system, except that a lamp in the shape of a band or strip may be part of an interdependent lamp system.

Two lamps or an even number of lamps in the shape of a band or strip shall be placed symmetrically in relation to the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle, extending on both sides to within at least 0.4 m of the extreme outer edge of the vehicle.
Two lamps or an even number of lamps in the shape of a band or strip shall be not less than 0.8 m long.
The illumination of a lamp in the shape of a band or strip shall be provided by not less than two light sources placed as close as possible to the ends.

The light-emitting surface of a lamp in the shape of a band or strip may be constituted by a number of juxtaposed elements on condition that these individual light-emitting surfaces, when projected on a transverse plane, fulfil the requirements of paragraph 5.7.2.1.

While specific instructions are absent, the lamp shall not intentionally vary its photometric characteristics (e.g. intensity, colour, apparent surface, etc.) during the period when the lamp is switched ON.
Direction-indicator lamps shall be flashing lamps.
Amber side-marker lamps complying with paragraph 6.18.7. shall be flashing lamps.
The vehicle-hazard warning signal shall be a flashing signal.
The emergency stop signal shall be a flashing signal.

When the photometric characteristics of any lamp vary in relation to the ambient light, as a consequence of other lamps being switched ON or OFF, or when the lamp is being used to provide another lighting function, the lamp shall ensure any variation in the photometric characteristics is in compliance with the technical provisions for the lamp concerned.
White light emitted by a lamp fitted on the front of the vehicle (as defined in paragraph 2.1.5.) shall not be visible from the rear of the vehicle.

For the visibility of red light towards the front of a vehicle, with the exception of a red rearmost side-marker lamp, there shall be no direct visibility of the apparent surface of a red lamp if viewed by an observer moving within Zone 1 in a transverse plane situated 25 m in front of the vehicle (see Annex 4).

For the visibility of white light towards the rear of a vehicle, with the exception of reversing lamps and white side conspicuity markings, there shall be no direct visibility of the apparent surface of a white lamp if viewed by an observer moving within Zone 2 in a transverse plane situated 25 m behind the vehicle (see Annex 4).

When there is doubt, the requirement that no red light shall be emitted to the front and no white light shall be emitted to the rear shall be deemed fulfilled if the luminous intensity of the red light emitted to the front and/or the white light emitted to the rear, as verified during type approval of the lamps, is not more than 0.25 cd per lamp taking into account the influence of the vehicle body if applicable.

The electrical connections shall be such that the front and rear position lamps, the end-outline marker lamps, if they exist, the side-marker lamps, if they exist, and the rear registration plate lamp can only be switched ON and OFF simultaneously.
In the case of an interdependent lamp system, all light sources shall be switched ON and OFF simultaneously.
The concealment of lamps shall be prohibited, with the exception of the main-beam headlamps, the dipped-beam headlamps and the front fog lamps, which may be concealed when they are not in use.
The direction-indicator lamp shall emit amber light.

The side-marker lamp shall emit amber light; however the rearmost side-marker lamp can be red if it is grouped or combined or reciprocally incorporated with the rear position lamp, the rear end-outline marker lamp, the rear fog lamp, the stop lamp or is grouped or has part of the light emitting surface in common with the rear retro-reflector.
The parking lamp shall emit white light in front and red light at the rear, and amber light if reciprocally incorporated in the side direction-indicator lamps or in the side-marker lamps.
The conspicuity marking shall emit white or yellow light to the side.

The voltage supplied at the terminals of devices which, according to their type approval documentation, have been tested by the application of a special power supply/electronic light source control gear, or in a secondary operating mode or at a voltage requested by the applicant, shall not exceed the voltage specified for the relevant devices or functions as they have been approved.

In all cases of electric power supply conditions not covered by paragraph 5.27.1., the voltage at the terminals of the device(s) or function(s) shall not exceed 6.75 V (6 Volt-Systems), 13.5 V (12 Volt-Systems) or 28 V (24 Volt-Systems) by more than 3 per cent, except that this requirement shall not apply to devices which include an electronic light source control gear, a variable intensity control being part of the device, or only light source(s) approved according to UN Regulation No. 128.
The means of controlling the maximum voltage at the terminals of the device(s) or function(s) may, for convenience, be located within the body of the device.

There shall be no obstacle on the inside of the angles of geometric visibility to the propagation of light from any part of the apparent surface of the lamp observed from infinity; no account is taken of obstacles that were already present when the lamp was type-approved.

If, when the lamp is installed, any part of the apparent surface of the lamp is hidden by any further parts of the vehicle, the part of the lamp not hidden by obstacles shall still conform to the photometric values prescribed for the approval of the device.
In the case of an interdependent lamp system, the geometric visibility requirements shall be fulfilled when all its interdependent lamps are operated together.

The lamps (devices) shall be type approved according to the corresponding device Regulations as specified in the relevant subparagraphs of paragraph 6 of this Regulation when installed on a vehicle, where applicable.
Light-signalling lamps incorporating a manufacturer logo shall be type approved according to the requirements of UN Regulation No. 148.
Side-marker lamps shall be mandatory on all vehicles the length of which exceeds 6 m, except for chassis-cabs.
The SM1 type of side-marker lamp shall be used on all categories of vehicles; however the SM2 type of side-marker lamps may be used on the M1 category of vehicles.

On M1 and N1 category vehicles less than 6 m in length, side-marker lamps shall be used, if they supplement the reduced geometric visibility requirements of front position lamps conforming to paragraph 6.9.5.2. and rear position lamps conforming to paragraph 6.10.5.2.
Side-marker lamps may be used on all other vehicles, where the SM1 or SM2 types of side-marker lamps may be used.
The minimum number of side-marker lamps per side shall be such that the rules for longitudinal positioning are complied with.
Side-marker lamps shall be type-approved according to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 91, or to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148.
The foremost side-marker lamp shall not be further than 3 m (4 m for semi-trailers) from the front of the vehicle.
In length, at least one side-marker lamp shall be fitted to the middle third of the vehicle.

The distance between two adjacent side-marker lamps shall not exceed 3 m, except that if the structure, design or the operational use of the vehicle makes it impossible to comply with such a requirement, this distance may be increased to 4 m.
The distance between the rearmost side-marker lamp and the rear of the vehicle shall not exceed 1 m.

For vehicles the length of which does not exceed 6 m and for chassis-cabs, it shall be sufficient to have one side-marker lamp fitted within the first third and/or within the last third of the vehicle length.

For M1 vehicles the length of which exceeds 6 m but does not exceed 7 m, it shall be sufficient to have one side-marker lamp fitted not further than 3 m from the front and one within the last third of the vehicle length.

The side-marker lamp shall be geometrically visible through a horizontal angle of 45° to the front and to the rear; however, for vehicles on which the installation of the side-marker lamps is optional, this value may be reduced to 30°.

Where side-marker lamps are used to supplement the reduced geometric visibility of front and rear direction indicator lamps conforming to paragraph 6.5.5.2. and/or position lamps conforming to paragraphs 6.9.5.2. and 6.10.5.2., the angles shall be 45° towards the front and rear ends of the vehicle and 30° towards the centre of the vehicle.

The side-marker lamp shall be geometrically visible within 10° above and below the horizontal; however, where a lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1.), the downward angle of 10° may be reduced to 5°.

Amber side-marker lamps may be wired to flash on M1 and N1 category vehicles less than 6 m in length, provided that this flashing is in phase and at the same frequency with the direction-indicator lamps at the same side of the vehicle.

When an optional side-marker lamp is grouped or combined with a position lamp that is reciprocally incorporated or grouped with the direction indicator, the side-marker lamp on the relevant side of the vehicle may be switched OFF during the entire period (both ON and OFF cycle) of activation of the direction indicator lamp.

When the rearmost side-marker lamp is combined with the rear position lamp reciprocally incorporated with the rear fog-lamp or stop lamp, the photometric characteristics of the side-marker lamp may be modified during the entire time the rear fog lamp or stop lamp is switched ON.
Rear side-marker lamps shall be amber if they flash with the rear direction-indicator lamp.

Where the lower bumper height at the test position is less than 425 mm, or is at least 425 mm and less than 500 mm and the manufacturer chooses paragraph 5.1.1., the absolute value of the maximum dynamic medial collateral ligament elongation at the knee measured when tested in accordance with Annex 5, paragraph 1. (Flexible lower legform impactor) shall not exceed 22 mm.

Where the lower bumper height at the test position is less than 425 mm, or is at least 425 mm and less than 500 mm and the manufacturer chooses paragraph 5.1.1., the maximum dynamic anterior cruciate ligament and posterior cruciate ligament elongation measured when tested in accordance with Annex 5, paragraph 1. (Flexible lower legform impactor) shall not exceed 13 mm.

Where the lower bumper height at the test position is less than 425 mm, or is at least 425 mm and less than 500 mm and the manufacturer chooses paragraph 5.1.1., the absolute value of the dynamic bending moment at the tibia measured when tested in accordance with Annex 5, paragraph 1. (Flexible lower legform impactor) shall not exceed 340 Nm.

Where the lower bumper height at the test position is less than 425 mm, or is at least 425 mm and less than 500 mm and the manufacturer chooses paragraph 5.1.1., where the manufacturer nominates bumper test widths up to a maximum of 264 mm in total, the absolute value of the tibia bending moment shall not exceed 380 Nm.
The flexible lower legform impactor shall be certified pursuant to Annex 6, paragraph 1.

Where the lower bumper height at the test position is at least 425 mm and less than 500 mm and the manufacturer chooses paragraph 5.1.2., or the lower bumper height at the test position is at least 500 mm, the instantaneous sum of the impact forces with respect to time measured when tested in accordance with Annex 5, paragraph 2. (upper legform to bumper) shall not exceed 7.5 kN.

Where the lower bumper height at the test position is at least 425 mm and less than 500 mm and the manufacturer chooses paragraph 5.1.2., or the lower bumper height at the test position is at least 500 mm, the bending moment on the test impactor measured when tested in accordance with Annex 5, paragraph 2. (upper legform to bumper) shall not exceed 510 Nm.
The upper legform impactor shall be certified pursuant to Annex 6, paragraph 2.
Devices designed to protect vulnerable road users when impacted by the vehicle shall be correctly activated before and/or be active during the relevant test.
Devices designed to protect vulnerable road users when impacted by the vehicle shall act as intended in a pedestrian impact.
When tested with the flexible lower legform impactor, the impact velocity of the impactor when striking the bumper shall be 11.1 m/s ± 0.2 m/s.
When tested with the flexible lower legform impactor, the effect of gravity shall be taken into account when the impact velocity is obtained from measurements taken before the time of first contact.
When tested with the flexible lower legform impactor, the tibia bending moments shall not exceed +/- 15 Nm within an evaluation interval of 30 ms immediately prior to impact.
When tested with the upper legform impactor, the impact velocity of the upper legform impactor when striking the bumper shall be 11.1 m/s ± 0.2 m/s.
Every device belonging to an approved type shall comprise a space of sufficient size for the approval marking and other markings as defined in paragraphs 3.3.3.2. to 3.3.3.6.
The markings shall be clearly legible and indelible.
The value for ‘a’ shall be at least 5 mm with regard to the size of the approval marking.
The four to six-digit sequential number, being part of the approval number prescribed in paragraph 3.2.3.2., shall be placed close to the approval mark.
In the case of front or rear position lamps, front or rear end-outline marker lamps, the arrow shall be directed outwards from the vehicle.
The arrow shall be directed outwards from the vehicle in the case of reversing lamps in case of reduced light distribution of two reversing lamps.
The arrow shall be directed towards the front of the vehicle in the case of direction indicators of categories 5 and 6 and combined parking lamps.
For direction indicators of category 6 an indication "R" or "L" shall be shown on the lamp, indicating the right or left side of the vehicle.

If applicable, the lamp shall bear, to the right side of the symbol mentioned in paragraph 3.2.4., the additional letter "D" where the lamp may be used as part of an assembly of two independent lamps.
If applicable, the lamp shall bear, to the right side of the symbol mentioned in paragraph 3.2.4., the additional letter "Y" where the lamp is used as part of an interdependent lamps system.
The lamps shall bear the approval marking.
The lamps shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant.
The lamp with replaceable light sources shall bear a marking indicating the category or categories of light source(s) prescribed.
Where the lamp has been approved for LED substitute light source(s), the lamp shall bear a marking indicating also the category or categories of the LED substitute light source(s).

Lamps with an electronic light source control gear, and/or a variable luminous intensity control, and/or a secondary operating mode, and/or non-replaceable light sources shall bear marking of the rated voltage(s) (i.e. 6V, 12V or 24V) or the range of voltage.
The light source module(s) shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant in case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used.
The light source module(s) shall bear the specific identification code of the module where replaceable light source module(s) is/are used.

The specific identification code of the module shall comprise the starting letters “MD” for “MODULE” followed by the approval mark without the circle as prescribed in paragraph 3.3.2.1.1, in case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used.

Where replaceable light source module(s) is/are used and several non-identical light source modules are used, the specific identification code of the module shall be followed by additional symbols or characters.

The light source module and the lamp shall both have marks from the same applicant, where the approval mark on the light source module does not have to be the same as the one on the lamp in which the module is used, in case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used.
The light source module(s) shall bear the rated voltage(s) or the range of voltage in case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used.
The lamp shall bear the specific identification code of the module as prescribed in paragraph 3.3.3.5. (a), (ii) in case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used.
The lamp shall bear the rated voltage(s) or the range of voltage in case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used.

An electronic light source control gear or variable luminous intensity control being part of the lamp, but not included into the lamp body, shall be marked with its identification number and the name of the manufacturer.
The approval marking shall be placed on an inner or outer part (transparent or not) of the lamp which is not designed to be separated from the transparent part of the lamp emitting the light.

When the lamp is fitted on the vehicle or when a movable part such as the hood or boot lid or a door is opened, the approval marking as well as the category or categories of LED substitute light source(s) prescribed, if any, shall be visible.
The approval marking shall be placed on both, the detachable lens and the main body, if the outer lens of a device is designed to be separated from the main body.
The main body of each device shall bear only the approval marking of the function(s) of that device in case an outer lens is used for several devices and bearing different approval markings.
The approval marking and the markings in paragraphs 3.3.3.2., 3.3.3.3., 3.3.3.4., 3.3.3.5. (b) and 3.3.3.6. shall be affixed on the lamp.
The component shall have the markings in paragraphs 3.3.3.5.(a) affixed on it.

The size of the components of a single approval mark shall not be less than the minimum size required for the smallest of the individual marks by the pertinent UN Regulations under which approval has been granted.

The requirements contained in sections 5 "General specifications" and 6 "Individual specifications" (and in the Annexes referenced in the said sections) of UN Regulations Nos. 48, 53, 74 or 86, and their series of amendments in force at the time of application for the lamp type approval, shall apply to UN Regulation No. 148.

The requirements pertinent to each lamp and to the category/ies of vehicle on which the lamp is intended to be installed shall be applied, where its verification at the moment of lamp type approval is feasible.

The lamps shall be so designed and constructed that in normal conditions of use, and notwithstanding the vibrations to which the lamps may be subjected in such use, the satisfactory operation of the lamps remains assured and the lamps retain the characteristics prescribed by this Regulation.

The internal structure of the optical components and/or the texture of the outer lens inside of the apparent surface of a lamp (function) shall fulfill all requirements for the specific function of this Regulation when incorporating only one manufacturer logo built by transparent or non-transparent components on request of the applicant.

The internal structure of the optical components and/or the texture of the outer lens inside of the apparent surface of a lamp (function) shall incorporate only the logo of the brand name of the vehicle manufacturer or the body manufacturer, irrespective of the marking requirements in paragraph 3.3., when incorporating only one manufacturer logo built by transparent or non-transparent components on request of the applicant.

The enclosed light emitting surface of the logo (incorporating transparent and non-transparent components of the logo) of a lamp, where the internal structure of the optical components and/or the texture of the outer lens inside of the apparent surface of the lamp incorporates only one manufacturer logo built by transparent or non-transparent components on request of the applicant, shall not exceed 100 cm2 in the direction of the reference axis.

The logo light emitting surface (incorporating transparent and non-transparent components of the logo) shall not be required to be symmetrical by itself, notwithstanding the requirements of paragraph 5.5.2. of UN Regulation No. 48, when the internal structure of the optical components and/or the texture of the outer lens inside of the apparent surface of a lamp (function) incorporates only one manufacturer logo built by transparent or non-transparent components on request of the applicant.
Stop lamps, direction indicator lamps, and reversing lamps shall not incorporate a logo.

If any one light source in a single lamp containing more than one light source fails, then the single lamp shall ensure that at least one of the following provisions applies: (a) the light intensity complies with the minimum intensity required in the pertinent table of standard light distribution as shown in Annex 3 and when all light sources are illuminated the maximum intensities shall not be exceeded; or (b) a signal for activation of a tell-tale indicating failure, as indicated in paragraphs 6.4.8., 6.7.8., 6.9.8, 6.10.8., 6.11.8., 6.12.8., 6.13.8. and 6.18.8. of UN Regulation No. 48, is produced.

The lamp shall only be equipped with replaceable light source(s) approved according to UN Regulations Nos. 37, 99 and/or 128, provided that no restriction on the use is made at the time of application for type approval, and/or light source module(s) and/or non-replaceable light source(s).
In case of replaceable UN approved light source(s), the design of the lamp shall be such that the light source(s) can be fixed in no other position but the correct one.
In case of replaceable UN approved light source(s), the light source(s) holder shall conform to the characteristics given in IEC Publication 60061.
The Light Signalling Devices shall not generate radiated or power line disturbances, which cause a malfunction of other electric/electronic systems of the vehicle.
In case of replaceable light source module(s), the design of the light source module(s) shall be such that the light source module(s) can only be fitted in the designated and correct position.
The design of the light source module(s) shall be such that the light source module(s) can only be removed with the use of tool(s) in case of replaceable light source module(s).
The design of the light source module(s) shall be such that the light source module(s) is tamperproof in case of replaceable light source module(s).

The design of the light source module(s) shall be such that regardless of the use of tool(s), the light source module(s) is not interchangeable with any replaceable UN approved light source and/or any other replaceable light source module having different characteristics that is located in the same lamp housing.

When the light source module is removed and replaced by another module provided by the applicant and bearing the same light source module identification code, in case of replaceable light source module(s), the device shall meet the photometric requirements.
Unless otherwise specified, the lamp shall be operated for testing at a supply voltage at the lamp of 6.75 V (6 Volt systems), 13.5 V (12 Volt systems) or 28 V (24 Volt systems).

The intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples supplied shall, if not otherwise specified, on the reference axis (HV), be not less than the minimum specified in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5.

The intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples supplied shall, if not otherwise specified and in no direction where the lamp is visible, not exceed the maximum specified in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5.

The intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples supplied shall, if not otherwise specified, outside the reference axis, be not less than the product of the minimum specified in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5., by the percentage specified in the pertinent light distribution figure reproduced in Annex 3 for each direction in question, or be not less than the intensity value as specified in the pertinent light distribution figure reproduced in Annex 3 for each direction in question.

The intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples supplied shall, if not otherwise specified and within the angles of geometric visibility defined in the tables in Annex 2, be not less than the minimum specified in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5.
The intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples supplied shall be observed in accordance with the provisions of the relevant paragraphs of Annex 3 on local variations of intensity.
The colour of the light emitted shall be measured inside the field of the light distribution grid defined for the specific function in the relevant paragraph of Annex 3.
The lamp shall exhibit no sharp variation of colour outside the field of the light distribution grid defined for the specific function in the relevant paragraph of Annex 3.
The direction indicator lamp of category 5 shall meet the minimum luminous intensity of 6∙10-1 cd in direction A according to Annex 2, as required in Table 8.
The direction indicator lamp of category 6 shall meet the minimum luminous intensity of 5.0∙101 cd in direction A according to Annex 2, as required in Table 8.
When used as a single lamp, the direction indicator lamp of categories 5 and 6 shall not exceed the maximum luminous intensity of 2.80∙102 cd as required in Table 8.
When marked "D", the direction indicator lamp of categories 5 and 6 shall not exceed the maximum luminous intensity of 1.40∙102 cd as required in Table 8.

The direction indicator lamp of categories 1, 1a, 1b, 2a, 2b, 11, 11a, 11b, 11c and 12 shall meet the minimum luminous intensity in the reference axis given for its category in Table 8, and the light emitted by each of the two samples supplied shall meet the requirements in Table 8.

For direction indicator lamps of categories 1, 1a, 1b, 2a, 2b, 11, 11a, 11b, 11c or 12, the flash may be produced by sequential activation of their light sources only if each light source, after its activation, remains lit until the end of the ON cycle.

For direction indicator lamps of categories 1, 1a, 1b, 2a, 2b, 11, 11a, 11b, 11c or 12, the flash may be produced by sequential activation of their light sources only if the sequence of activation of the light sources produces a signal which proceeds in a uniform progressive manner from inboard towards the outboard edge of the light emitting surface.

For direction indicator lamps of categories 1, 1a, 1b, 2a, 2b, 11, 11a, 11b, 11c or 12, the flash may be produced by sequential activation of their light sources only if it is one signal with no interruption and no vertical oscillations (e.g. not more than one change of direction along the vertical axis), and the distance between two adjacent/tangential distinct parts of the light emitting surface of the sequential direction indicator does not exceed 50mm when measured perpendicularly to the reference axis, instead of the values defined in paragraph 5.7.2. of UN Regulation No. 48 or paragraph 5.7.2. of UN Regulation No. 86 or paragraph 5.6.2. of UN Regulation No. 53.

For direction indicator lamps of categories 1, 1a, 1b, 2a, 2b, 11, 11a, 11b, 11c or 12, the flash may be produced by sequential activation of their light sources only if the interruptions of the signal do not create any overlap in the vertical axis between the different parts, from inboard towards the outboard of the vehicle, and are not used for any other lighting or light signalling functions.

For direction indicator lamps of categories 1, 1a, 1b, 2a, 2b, 11, 11a, 11b, 11c or 12, the flash may be produced by sequential activation of their light sources only if the variation finishes no more than 200ms after the beginning of the ON cycle.

For direction indicator lamps of categories 1, 1a, 1b, 2a, 2b, 11, 11a, 11b, 11c or 12, the flash may be produced by sequential activation of their light sources only if the orthogonal projection of the light emitting surfaces of the direction indicator in the direction of the axis of reference is circumscribed by a rectangle on a plane normal to the axis of reference and having its longer sides parallel to the H-plane, with the ratio of the horizontal to the vertical sides not less than 1.7.

For direction indicator lamps of categories 1, 1a, 1b, 2a, 2b, 11, 11a, 11b, 11c or 12 whose flash is produced by sequential activation of their light sources, compliance with the conditions of paragraph 5.6.5 (a) to (e) shall be verified in flashing mode.
The colour of the light emitted by the direction indicator lamp shall be amber.
The light emitted by each sample of the device shall meet the requirements in Table 9.

For red side marker lamps, in the angular field from 60° to 90° in horizontal direction and ±20° in vertical direction towards the front of the vehicle, the maximum intensity shall be limited to 2.5∙10-1 cd.
The colour of the light emitted by the device shall be amber.

The colour of the light emitted by the device may be red only if the rearmost side marker lamp is grouped or combined or reciprocally incorporated with the rear position lamp, the rear end-outline marker lamp, the rear fog lamp, the stop lamp, or is grouped with or has part of the light emitting surface in common with the rear retro-reflector.

Where a front or rear direction indicator lamp, front or rear position lamp, front or rear end-outline marker lamp, parking lamp, stop lamp of category S1, S2 or MS, or side marker lamp is intended to be installed at a mounting height (using the H plane specified by the manufacturer) equal to or less than 750 mm above the ground, the photometric intensity shall be verified only up to an angle of 5° downwards.

The light intensity in each direction of a part of the field formed by the grid lines shall meet at least the lowest minimum value being shown on the grid lines surrounding the questioned direction as a percentage, within the field of light distribution schematically shown as a grid.

When visual examination of a reversing lamp appears to reveal substantial local variations of intensity, no intensity measured between two of the directions of measurement of the grid shall be below 50 per cent of the lower minimum intensity of the two prescribed for these directions.

The luminous intensities for all other lamps (other than those mentioned in 1.2.1), measured after 1 min and either after 30 minutes of operation, or after photometric stability has occurred, shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.

The luminous intensity distribution shall, depending on the light source technology and in addition to paragraph 1, be checked for compliance at the point in time listed in Table A8-1, where the luminous intensity distributions at a point in time may be calculated from the luminous intensity distribution measured according to paragraph 1 by applying at each test point the ratio of luminous intensities measured at the reference coordinate of the lamp (function) under consideration.
For vehicles with a lower bumper height of less than 425 mm, the requirements of paragraph 4.1.1. shall be applied.

For vehicles with a lower bumper height which is greater than, or equal to 425 mm and less than 500 mm, the requirements of either paragraph 4.1.1. or 4.1.2., at the choice of the manufacturer, shall be applied.
For vehicles with a lower bumper height of greater than, or equal to, 500 mm, the requirements of paragraph 4.1.2. shall be applied.

When tested in accordance with paragraph 7.1.1. (flexible lower legform to bumper), the absolute value of the maximum dynamic medial collateral ligament elongation at the knee of the vehicle bumper shall not exceed 22 mm.

When tested in accordance with paragraph 7.1.1. (flexible lower legform to bumper), the maximum dynamic anterior cruciate ligament and posterior cruciate ligament elongation of the vehicle bumper shall not exceed 13 mm.
When tested in accordance with paragraph 7.1.1. (flexible lower legform to bumper), the absolute value of dynamic bending moments at the tibia shall not exceed 340 Nm.

When tested in accordance with paragraph 7.1.1. (flexible lower legform to bumper), where the manufacturer nominates bumper test widths up to a maximum of 264 mm in total, the absolute value of the tibia bending moment shall not exceed 380 Nm.
When tested in accordance with paragraph 7.1.2. (upper legform to bumper), the instantaneous sum of the impact forces with respect to time shall not exceed 7.5 kN.
When tested in accordance with paragraph 7.1.2. (upper legform to bumper), the bending moment on the test impactor shall not exceed 510 Nm.
All devices designed to protect vulnerable road users when impacted by the vehicle shall be correctly activated before and/or be active during the relevant test.

For vehicle components which could change shape or position, other than active devices to protect pedestrians, and which have more than one fixed shape or position, the components shall comply with the applicable requirements in each fixed shape or position.
The impact velocity of the impactor when striking the bumper shall be 11.1 ± 0.2 m/s.
The effect of gravity shall be taken into account when the impact velocity of the impactor is obtained from measurements taken before the time of first contact.
The tibia bending moments shall not exceed ± 15 Nm within an evaluation interval of 30 ms immediately prior to impact.
The impact velocity of the upper legform impactor when striking the bumper shall be 11.1 ± 0.2 m/s.

Where a vehicle or electrical/electronic system or ESA does not include an electronic oscillator with an operating frequency greater than 9 kHz, the vehicle or electrical/electronic system or ESA shall be deemed to comply with paragraph 6.3.2. or 6.6.2. and with Annexes 5 and 8.

The ESAs that are not switched, contain no switches or do not include inductive load shall be deemed to comply with paragraph 6.7, except that they need not be tested for transient conducted emission.
The lamps which cannot be mounted on either side of the vehicle indiscriminately shall be provided with a horizontal arrow showing in which position the lamp is to be mounted.
The lamp equipped with light source module(s) or non-replaceable light source(s) shall have all measurements made with the light source(s) present in the lamp.
The measured values shall not deviate unfavourably by more than 20 per cent from the values prescribed in this Regulation.
The measured values shall correspond to the values shown in Table 12 for the minimum values required throughout the fields specified in Annexes 2 and 3.
Arrangement "A" shall apply to all motor vehicles.

The height of the light-emitting surface of the side direction-indicator lamps of categories 5 or 6 shall not be: Less than: 350 mm for M1 and N1 category of vehicles, and 500 mm for all other categories of vehicles, both measured from the lowest point; and More than: 1,500 mm, measured from the highest point.

The distance between the light-emitting surface of the side direction-indicator lamp (categories 5 and 6) and the transverse plane which marks the forward boundary of the vehicle's overall length, shall not exceed 1,800 mm.
However, this distance shall not exceed 2,500 mm for M1 and N1 category vehicles.
Where a lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1), the downward angle of 15° may be reduced to 5°.
To be considered visible, the lamp shall provide an unobstructed view of the apparent surface of at least 12.5 square centimetres, except for side direction-indicators of categories 5 and 6.
Direction-indicator lamps shall switch ON independently of the other lamps.
All direction-indicator lamps on one side of a vehicle shall be switched ON and OFF automatically as defined by applicable UN Regulations and/or by means of one control and shall flash in phase.

On M1 and N1 vehicles less than 6 m in length, with an arrangement complying with paragraph 6.5.5.2. above, the amber side-marker lamps, when mounted, shall also flash at the same frequency (in phase) with the direction- indicator lamps.
A direction indicator capable of being activated in different modes (static or sequential), shall not switch between both modes once activated.
The light shall be a flashing light flashing 90 ± 30 times per minute.
Operation of the light-signal control shall be followed within not more than one second by the emission of light and within not more than one and one-half seconds by its first extinction.
In the event of failure, other than short-circuit, of one direction-indicator lamp, the others shall continue to flash, but the frequency in this condition may be different from that prescribed.
The total response time (TRT) of the pedestrian impact sensing system shall be confirmed by using the FlexPLI at a vehicle speed of 11.1 m/s and at the vehicle centreline (Y0).
The number of lamps mounted on the vehicle shall be equal to the number indicated in the individual specifications of this Regulation.

For M1 and N1 category vehicles, as an alternative to paragraph 6.9.5.1, at the discretion of the manufacturer or his duly accredited representative, and only if a front side-marker lamp is installed on the vehicle, the horizontal angle shall be 45° outwards to 45° inwards.
For a front side-marker lamp used under paragraph 6.9.5.2, the vertical angle shall be 15° above and 15° below the horizontal.
The illuminating surface area of any retro-reflector that does not transmit light shall be excluded from the apparent surface of the front side-marker lamp.
For vehicles with a lower bumper height at the test position of greater than, or equal to, 500 mm the requirements of paragraph 5.1.2. shall be applied.

For vehicle components which could change shape or position, other than active devices to protect pedestrians, and which have more than one fixed shape or position shall require the vehicle to comply with the components in each fixed shape or position.

When the vertical angle of geometric visibility below the horizontal is reduced to 5º (lamp at less than 750 mm above the ground measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1. above), the photometric field of measurements of the installed optical unit shall be permitted to be reduced to 5º below the horizontal.

The position lamps or daytime running lamps, which are reciprocally incorporated with another function, using a common light source, and designed to operate permanently with an additional system to regulate the intensity of the light emitted, shall be permitted.

Sensors, cameras, radar devices, etc. being part of driver assist systems may become damaged, disoriented or broken due to an impact carried out according to Annex 3 as long as the basic braking and steering performance are still intact.
The side direction-indicator lamps of category 5 shall provide a vertical visibility angle of 15° above and below the horizontal.
The value of 5° given for dead angle of visibility to the rear of the side direction-indicator is an upper limit d ≤ 1.80 m (for M1 and N1 category vehicles d ≤ 2.50 m).

Where a lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1), for the direction indicator lamps of categories 1, 1a, 1b, 2a and 2b the inward angle of 45° may be reduced to 20° under the H plane.

For M1 and N1 category vehicles, at the discretion of the manufacturer, front and rear direction-indicator lamps and side-marker lamps may be installed, provided the horizontal angles are as shown in the figure in paragraph 6.5.
The vertical angles of the direction-indicator lamps shall be 15° above and 15° below the horizontal.

In case of replaceable UN approved light source(s), where a category of LED substitute light source(s) is also prescribed, the light source(s) holder shall conform to the holder data sheet relevant to the category of LED substitute light source(s).
